name: AutoML
limitations: Not included as built-in library in Databricks Runtime 18.0 ML or above; requires network ports 1017 and 1021 open; unsupported on Standard (shared) compute access mode; no additional libraries beyond preinstalled ML runtime allowed; library modifications cause run failures
blurb: Quickly baseline models for problems like readmission or churn on tabular claims data.

name: Feature Store / Engineering
limitations: Requires Unity Catalog enabled workspace; legacy Workspace Feature Store is deprecated
blurb: Build and reuse governed features — e.g., member utilization history — consistently across training and serving. Prevents train/serve skew in risk models.

name: ML Runtime
blurb: Preconfigured, governed environments so data scientists spend time on models, not setup.

name: MLflow
blurb: The system of record for training, versioning, and governing ML models like risk and readmission predictors. Approved for the enterprise model lifecycle.

name: Model Serving
limitations: 1000 endpoints per workspace; 300K QPS per endpoint/workspace with route optimization; 16 MB payload limit (4 MB for agents); requests/responses >1 MB not logged; 597s max execution time; 50 create/update ops per 5 min; limited region availability
objections: Reviewing network isolation + audit logging for PHI scoring.
blurb: Serve models as low-latency APIs — e.g., real-time risk or fraud scoring on incoming claims. Under review for network isolation and audit logging before scoring PHI.

name: Serverless GPU / AI Runtime
blurb: On-demand GPU compute for training or fine-tuning without managing clusters.

name: Vector Search
limitations: Requires Unity Catalog and serverless compute; standard endpoints need change data feed; struct/map column restrictions; no row/column level permissions; no cross-workspace cloning; max 4096 embedding dimensions; max 50 indexes per endpoint; hybrid search limited to 200 results
blurb: Semantic search over clinical notes, policies, and provider documents to power RAG assistants. Lets staff find relevant guidance across unstructured corpora.

name: Feature tables
limitations: Requires Unity Catalog enabled workspace
blurb: Store curated member and provider features for reuse across many models.

name: Feature views
limitations: Requires workspace enabled for Unity Catalog
blurb: Define features declaratively so they stay consistent and governed.

name: Online tables / feature serving
blurb: Serve features at low latency for real-time scoring at the point of care.

name: MLflow 3 (logged models, deployment jobs)
blurb: Standardize how models move from training to production deployment.

name: Model Registry (UC-backed)
blurb: Govern model versions and approvals in Unity Catalog alongside the data they were trained on.

name: Trace storage in Unity Catalog
blurb: Keep unlimited governed traces of AI interactions for audit and quality review.

name: Tracing
blurb: Trace GenAI and model calls to debug and audit AI-assisted member workflows.

name: Tracking
blurb: Record every training run so model results for care-management scoring are reproducible and auditable.

name: Batch inference
blurb: Score large claims or member batches cost-effectively on a schedule.

name: Custom model endpoints
limitations: 1000 endpoints per workspace; 300K QPS per endpoint/workspace with route optimization; 1024 max provisioned concurrency per model; 16 MB payload limit; 597s max execution duration; requests/responses >1 MB not logged; 50 create/update ops per 5 min
blurb: Deploy the payer's own trained models (readmission, risk) behind governed endpoints.

name: External models
limitations: Resource and payload limits documented under Foundation Model APIs rate limits and quotas (separate page); no default PrivateLink support to external endpoints (per-region evaluation required)
blurb: Route to third-party model providers through one governed, logged gateway.

name: Foundation Model APIs (pay-per-token)
limitations: region availability varies, see Foundation models hosted on Databricks for specific regions
blurb: Call hosted LLMs on demand for summarization and extraction without managing infrastructure.

name: Provisioned throughput
limitations: Per model: 1024 max concurrency (with route optimization); Per workspace: 4096 max concurrency; Requires custom option and route optimization for max limits; Contact account team to increase limits
blurb: Reserve guaranteed LLM capacity for predictable, high-volume claims processing.

name: Delta sync index
limitations: Requires Unity Catalog and serverless compute; source table must use change data feed; row size limit 100KB; embedding source column limit 32,764 bytes; max 50 columns and 50 metadata fields per index; max embedding dimension 4096; struct/map column restrictions; no row/column level permissions
blurb: Keep the search index automatically in sync with governed source documents.

name: Direct index
limitations: Embeddings limited to ~2,000,000 at 768 dimension per standard endpoint; bulk upsert/delete request size limited to 10MB per index; struct/map columns have restrictions; row/column level permissions not supported; cannot clone index across workspaces
blurb: Manage embeddings directly when documents come from outside the lakehouse.

name: High-QPS endpoints
blurb: Support high-concurrency search for member- or provider-facing assistants.

name: Hybrid search
limitations: Maximum 200 results per query; query limited to 1024 words or 2-byte characters; not supported on storage-optimized endpoints
blurb: Combine keyword and semantic matching for better recall on clinical terminology.

name: Asset Bundles (DABs)
blurb: Deploy jobs, pipelines, and apps as versioned code for repeatable, auditable releases. Approved as the enterprise deployment standard.

name: Databricks Apps
limitations: Maximum 100 Databricks apps per workspace (fixed limit, cannot be increased)
objections: Reviewing app-level auth + egress for PHI apps.
blurb: Host internal data apps — like this tracker — directly on governed platform compute. Under review for app-level auth and egress before any PHI-bearing app.

name: Databricks CLI
blurb: Scriptable control of the platform for automation and this tracker's refresh job. Approved for platform-team tooling.

name: Databricks Connect
limitations: Only available for Databricks Runtime 13.3 LTS and above; limited to Python, R, and Scala languages
blurb: Develop against lakehouse data from local IDEs with governance intact.

name: Git folders (branches, CI/CD, private Git)
limitations: Working branches limited to 1GB; files >10MB not viewable in UI; each Git operation supports max 2GB memory and 4GB disk writes; SSH not supported (HTTPS only); GPG commit signing unsupported; standard Git submodules unsupported; MLflow experiments don't work in Git folders
blurb: Version-control notebooks and pipelines against the payer's enterprise Git for review and audit.

name: Notebooks (+ Genie Code)
blurb: The primary analysis surface for data scientists and analysts, now AI-assisted.

name: REST API
blurb: Programmatic access for custom integrations and governance automation.

name: SDKs (Python/Java/Go/JS/R)
blurb: Integrate Databricks into the payer's internal applications and automation.

name: Terraform provider
blurb: Manage workspaces and governance as infrastructure-as-code within existing pipelines.

name: VS Code / PyCharm extensions
limitations: R, Scala, and SQL notebooks can only be run as automated jobs; no deeper IDE support for these languages within VS Code
blurb: Let engineers build and run pipelines from their preferred IDE.

name: AppKit (TS/React)
blurb: Build modern React data apps for care-management and operations teams.

name: Horizontal scaling
blurb: Scale internal apps to more concurrent users as adoption grows.

name: User authorization (acts as user)
blurb: Apps enforce each user's own data permissions — important for PHI least-privilege.

name: Webhook-triggered deploys
blurb: Auto-deploy app updates from CI/CD for faster, safer releases.

name: Classic compute
blurb: Customer-managed clusters for workloads needing specific instance types or network controls. Approved where fine-grained control is required.

name: Lakeguard
blurb: Enforces Unity Catalog governance on shared clusters so data access stays controlled even in multi-user compute.

name: Photon
limitations: No UDF, RDD API, or Dataset API support; stateless streaming only; no benefit for queries under 2 seconds; Graviton instances with Photon don't support Container Services for dedicated compute or SQL warehouses
blurb: A vectorized engine that speeds up claims queries and cuts compute cost on large scans.

name: Predictive Optimization (zero-ops)
limitations: Does not run on tables loaded to workspace as OpenSharing recipients; Does not run on external tables; Only supports Unity Catalog managed tables (Delta Lake and Iceberg)
blurb: Databricks automatically tunes and compacts tables so the team doesn't hand-maintain them. Keeps the growing claims estate fast without ops overhead.

name: Serverless compute
limitations: R not supported; only Spark Connect APIs (no RDD); ANSI mode default; 128MB row limit; Unity Catalog required; limited DBFS access; UDFs can't access internet; no Spark UI; streaming limited to AvailableNow/Once triggers; 7-day max runtime; no caching APIs; Scala/R unsupported in notebooks
objections: PHI workloads require the compliance security profile enabled.
blurb: Fully managed, instantly elastic compute that cuts idle cost for bursty claims and reporting jobs. Approved with the condition that PHI workloads run with the compliance security profile enabled.

name: Autoscaling
blurb: Scale cluster size to the workload to balance performance and cost.

name: Cluster policies
blurb: Enforce cost and security guardrails on what compute teams can create.

name: Dedicated group clusters
blurb: Isolate a cluster to a specific team or sensitive workload.

name: Instance pools
blurb: Keep warm instances ready to cut cluster startup latency for recurring jobs.

name: Standard & dedicated clusters
blurb: General-purpose compute for engineering and data-science workloads.

name: Auto liquid clustering
limitations: Does not run on tables loaded as OpenSharing recipients; Does not run on external tables
blurb: New tables cluster themselves for performance with zero manual tuning.

name: Auto-optimize & auto compaction
limitations: Does not run on tables loaded as OpenSharing recipients; Does not run on external tables
blurb: Automatically keep table file sizes healthy for fast reads.

name: Automatic statistics
limitations: Does not run on tables loaded as OpenSharing recipients; Does not run on external tables
blurb: Keeps query-planner statistics current automatically for consistently fast queries.

name: JAR tasks on serverless
blurb: Run existing JVM claims-processing jobs on serverless once it reaches GA.

name: Serverless DLT
limitations: Continuous streaming triggers not supported (must use Trigger.AvailableNow or Trigger.Once); 7-day maximum runtime; UDFs cannot access internet; UDFs limited to 1GB memory; no Spark UI; no dataframe/SQL caching; ANSI mode enabled by default
blurb: Run declarative pipelines elastically, scaling to the size of each refresh.

name: Serverless GPU
blurb: On-demand GPUs for model training without managing GPU clusters.

name: Serverless SQL warehouses
blurb: Fast-starting warehouses for BI, scaled automatically to analyst demand.

name: Serverless jobs
limitations: R not supported; only Spark Connect APIs (no RDD); 7-day max runtime; no compute policies/init scripts/instance pools; streaming limited to AvailableNow/Once triggers; UDFs cannot access internet; no Spark UI; cross-workspace access restricted; task logs not isolated per run
blurb: Run scheduled claims pipelines without provisioning or paying for idle clusters.

name: Serverless notebooks
limitations: Scala and R not supported; JAR libraries not supported; notebook-scoped libraries not cached across sessions; no autocomplete or Variable Explorer for dataframes; TEMP tables/views not shared between users; must use .ipynb format; notebook tags not supported
blurb: Give analysts instant compute for exploration without waiting on cluster startup.

name: AI Functions (SQL)
limitations: Not available on Classic SQL warehouses; Requires Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS or above; Model inference may run on separate Databricks-managed infrastructure with additional billing
objections: Board reviewing which foundation models are approved for PHI prompts.
blurb: Call LLMs directly from SQL to classify, extract, and summarize at scale — e.g., categorize appeals letters. Under review to decide which foundation models are approved for PHI-bearing prompts.

name: AI Playground
limitations: Workspace must be in a region that supports Foundation Models; availability may require contacting Databricks account team; building agents in AI Playground is a legacy approach
blurb: Let the team prototype prompts safely before building a production assistant.

name: Agent Bricks
objections: Preview — internal/non-PHI eval only until GA.
blurb: Low-code building blocks for document Q&A and multi-agent assistants over governed content. Earmarked for the TRB document assistant, but Beta so internal/non-PHI evaluation only until GA.

name: Databricks-provided MCP (Slack/GitHub/Drive)
blurb: Ready-made connectors so internal assistants can reach common enterprise tools.

name: Foundation Model fine-tuning
blurb: Adapt a base model to payer-specific terminology (codes, plan names) for better accuracy.

name: GenAI Evaluation (LLM-as-judge)
blurb: Score AI answers for accuracy and safety — essential evidence for the TRB before any member-facing GenAI.

name: MCP servers
blurb: Expose governed tools and data to agents through a standard protocol.

name: Mosaic AI Agent Framework
blurb: Build governed, traceable AI agents over payer data — e.g., a prior-authorization assistant. The foundation for production GenAI with evaluation and logging built in.

name: Unity Gateway (AI governance)
limitations: Maximum 20 rate limits per service; maximum 5 group-specific rate limits per service; workspace must be in Unity Gateway supported region
blurb: A governance plane over all AI traffic — access control, guardrails, logging, and budgets. The control point the payer needs before broad LLM rollout.

name: Custom agents
blurb: Hand-build agents with full control over tools and guardrails for sensitive workflows.

name: Information Extraction
blurb: Pull structured fields out of unstructured clinical and claims documents at scale.

name: Knowledge Assistant
blurb: RAG assistant over policies and TRB minutes to answer objection and review-history questions.

name: Supervisor (Multi-Agent)
limitations: Beta Supervisor API EOL Sep 30 2026 — migrate to custom agents.
blurb: Orchestrate several specialized agents (claims, eligibility, policy) behind one assistant.

name: ai_classify / ai_extract / ai_summarize
limitations: Not available on Classic SQL warehouses; Requires Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS or above
blurb: Categorize correspondence, pull fields from documents, and summarize notes with one function call.

name: ai_forecast / ai_gen / ai_mask / ai_translate
limitations: Not available on Classic SQL warehouses; Requires Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS or above
blurb: Forecast utilization, generate text, mask PII, and translate member communications in SQL.

name: ai_parse_document
limitations: Not available on Classic SQL warehouses; Requires Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS or above
blurb: Turn scanned claims documents and EOBs into structured, queryable data.

name: ai_query
limitations: Not available on Classic SQL warehouses; Requires Databricks Runtime 15.4 LTS or above
blurb: Run an LLM over millions of claims rows in a single governed SQL statement.

name: Access control & guardrails
limitations: Maximum 20 rate limits per service; maximum 5 group-specific rate limits per service; workspace must be in Unity Gateway supported region
blurb: Enforce who can call which models and block unsafe or PHI-leaking prompts and responses.

name: Budgets
blurb: Cap AI spend per team to keep GenAI pilots within budget.

name: External service policies
limitations: Maximum 20 rate limits per service; maximum 5 group-specific rate limits per service; rate limiter may allow short bursts above configured limit due to concurrent request handling and independent enforcement across service instances

name: Model / MCP / Provider services
limitations: Maximum 20 rate limits per service; maximum 5 group-specific rate limits per service; requires workspace in Unity Gateway supported region
blurb: Centrally register approved models and providers for governed reuse.

name: Observability
blurb: Monitor AI usage, latency, and cost across teams in one place.

name: Traffic management & failover
blurb: Route and fail over LLM traffic for reliable member-facing experiences.

name: Auto Loader
blurb: Incrementally ingest files as they land in cloud storage, with no manual bookkeeping. Ideal for continuous 837 EDI claim drops and daily eligibility files.

name: COPY INTO
limitations: Deletion vectors enabled by COPY INTO block queries on Databricks Runtime 11.3 LTS and below; requires account administrator to configure data access before use; schemaless table creation with mergeSchema requires Databricks Runtime 11.3 LTS and above
blurb: Idempotent bulk load of historical claims extracts into Delta — safe to re-run without duplicates.

name: Lakeflow Connect (managed connectors)
limitations: Serverless-only pipelines; coverage varies by source API.
blurb: Managed, serverless connectors that pull SaaS and database sources into the lakehouse. Lets the payer ingest CRM, HR, and claims systems without hand-built, hand-maintained pipelines.

name: Streaming ingest (Structured Streaming)
blurb: Battle-tested near-real-time ingestion for eligibility, authorization, and claims-status events.

name: Zerobus ingest
limitations: Availability limited to specific regions; requires client-side firewall allowlist configuration for IP addresses; requires service principal setup and table privileges
blurb: Direct, high-throughput event ingestion without standing up a broker. Promising for device/telemetry, but held until GA before any PHI use.

name: Directory listing mode
blurb: Simple file discovery for lower-volume claim-extract folders.

name: FILE / unstructured ingestion
blurb: Land clinical documents and images for downstream parsing and extraction.

name: File notification mode
limitations: Needs cloud event/IAM config.
blurb: Event-driven ingestion for high-volume claims landing zones where directory listing is too slow.

name: Schema inference & evolution
limitations: Column deletions handled manually.
blurb: Absorb new fields in partner feeds automatically without breaking the ingestion pipeline.

name: Confluence
blurb: Index internal policy and SOP pages so they can feed the TRB knowledge assistant.

name: Google Ads
blurb: Measure member-acquisition campaign performance during open enrollment.

name: Google Analytics 4
blurb: Analyze member-portal web engagement alongside claims to improve digital self-service.

name: Google Drive
limitations: SCD Type 2 not supported.
blurb: Ingest provider rosters and ad-hoc spreadsheets partners share via Drive.

name: Jira
blurb: Track engineering and compliance-remediation work as data for program reporting.

name: Kafka
limitations: No UI authoring; no SCD2; partial schema evolution.
blurb: Ingest streaming events such as real-time eligibility or authorization checks.

name: Meta Ads
blurb: Bring in social-campaign spend and conversions to analyze member-growth ROI.

name: MySQL CDC
limitations: Username/password auth only; max 250 tables/pipeline.
blurb: Capture changes from operational apps backed by MySQL, such as provider portals.

name: PostgreSQL CDC
limitations: Requires logical replication + replication slots.
blurb: Stream enrollment or eligibility changes from Postgres systems into the lakehouse.

name: Query-based connectors (cursor, no CDC)
blurb: Pull from sources without CDC via scheduled cursor reads, widening connector coverage.

name: RabbitMQ
blurb: Consume message-queue events from legacy integration buses between core systems.

name: SQL Server (cloud + on-prem)
limitations: CDC needs Enterprise edition; SQL Server 2012+.
blurb: CDC the core claims-adjudication EDW into the lakehouse near-real-time to offload reporting. Approved with standard network controls despite Public Preview status.

name: Salesforce
objections: Security reviewing OAuth scope + PII field mapping.
blurb: Sync Health Cloud / Service Cloud member and case data into the lakehouse to build a Member 360. Under review for OAuth scope and PII field handling.

name: ServiceNow
blurb: Bring IT and provider-services tickets in for operational and SLA analytics.

name: SharePoint
blurb: Pull care-management documents and provider contracts from SharePoint libraries into governed storage.

name: TikTok Ads
blurb: Track emerging-channel ad performance for younger member segments.

name: Workday
limitations: Incremental ingestion in Beta.
blurb: Analyze workforce and benefits-administration data for HR and staffing analytics.

name: Google Pub/Sub source
blurb: Stream events from GCP-hosted systems into the lakehouse.

name: Kafka source
blurb: Consume real-time event streams from the enterprise Kafka backbone.

name: Kinesis source
blurb: Ingest AWS-native event streams for near-real-time pipelines.

name: C# / .NET SDK
blurb: Write events directly from the payer's .NET line-of-business applications.

name: C++ SDK
blurb: Native ingestion from high-performance or embedded systems.

name: Kafka-compatible APIs
blurb: Point existing Kafka producers at Zerobus without rewriting them.

name: OpenTelemetry (OTLP)
limitations: Availability limited to specific workspace regions; requires client-side firewall allowlist configuration for Zerobus Ingest IP addresses
blurb: Ingest standardized telemetry/observability signals from the payer's apps.

name: REST API
limitations: Stateless interface best suited for lightweight or chatty edge devices rather than high-volume streaming; lower sustained throughput compared to SDK over gRPC option
blurb: Simple HTTP ingestion for remote-monitoring devices and lightweight clients.

name: gRPC SDK
limitations: Requires client-side firewall allowlist configuration for Zerobus Ingest IP addresses; availability limited by workspace region
blurb: Lowest-latency path for writing high-volume events directly from services.

name: Lakeflow Declarative Pipelines (DLT)
limitations: 1,000 concurrent pipeline updates per workspace; 1,000 datasets per pipeline; 100 source files or 50 source entries (files/folders) per pipeline; identity columns not supported with AUTO CDC; materialized views/streaming tables not accessible to external systems by default
blurb: Declarative medallion pipelines that build curated claims and member tables with built-in data-quality checks. The payer's standard for turning raw 837/835 feeds into trusted analytics tables.

name: Lakeflow Designer (no-code)
blurb: Lets analysts build pipelines visually, reducing the data-engineering backlog for simple feeds.

name: Lakeflow Jobs (Workflows)
limitations: 2000 concurrent task runs per workspace; 10000 jobs created per hour limit; 12000 saved jobs per workspace max; 1000 tasks per job max; 10000 character limit for job parameters when using dynamic values
blurb: The orchestration engine for every scheduled claims, eligibility, and reporting workload. Approved as the enterprise standard for production scheduling.

name: Structured Streaming
blurb: Build custom near-real-time transformations for eligibility and authorization events.

name: dbt integration
limitations: Requires dbt Cloud/Core.
blurb: Let analytics-engineering teams model claims data in dbt while running on governed Databricks compute.

name: APPLY CHANGES (SCD 1 & 2)
limitations: Identity columns not supported with tables that are target of AUTO CDC processing; Delta Lake time travel queries not supported with materialized views (only streaming tables)
blurb: Track member and provider history over time with proper slowly-changing-dimension handling.

name: Expectations (data quality)
limitations: SQL-only constraints; no custom Python.
blurb: Enforce rules like valid member IDs and non-null diagnosis codes, quarantining bad claims automatically.

name: Materialized views
limitations: Identity columns might be recomputed during updates; not accessible to external systems by default; Delta Lake time travel queries not supported; can only be target of single operation (no multi-write)
blurb: Incrementally refreshed gold tables for dashboards and quality measures.

name: New multi-file editor
limitations: 100 source file limit per pipeline when referencing individual files; 50 source entry limit when using folders; 1000 total file limit when using folders
blurb: Author larger pipelines across multiple files for better maintainability by the data-engineering team.

name: Serverless DLT
blurb: Run claims pipelines without managing clusters, paying only for what each refresh uses.

name: Sinks (Delta/Iceberg/Parquet)
blurb: Write curated outputs to the format partners and downstream tools expect.

name: Streaming tables
limitations: Identity columns might be recomputed during updates to materialized views, recommended only for streaming tables; Delta Lake time travel queries supported only with streaming tables, not materialized views; pivot() function not supported
blurb: Continuously updated bronze/silver tables for near-real-time claims and eligibility.

name: Table retention on delete (change)
blurb: Changes how data is retained when a table is dropped; review carefully before adoption to avoid unexpected PHI retention or loss.

name: Conditional (if/else) tasks
blurb: Branch a workflow — e.g., only run reconciliation when late claims arrive.

name: Continuous jobs
blurb: Keep near-real-time eligibility pipelines running without manual re-triggering.

name: For-each tasks
blurb: Fan out the same processing across many partners, plans, or regions in parallel.

name: Job-as-task
blurb: Compose large pipelines by nesting existing jobs as reusable building blocks.

name: Notebook / Python / SQL / dbt tasks
limitations: Workspace limited to 2000 concurrent task runs; max 10000 jobs created per hour per workspace; max 12000 saved jobs per workspace; max 1000 tasks per job; job parameters limited to 10000 characters when using dynamic values
blurb: Run any mix of task types in one claims pipeline without stitching tools together.

name: Pipeline tasks
blurb: Trigger DLT pipelines as steps within a larger orchestrated workflow.

name: Serverless jobs
limitations: Max 1000 tasks/job; startup latency.
blurb: Run scheduled claims pipelines as workflow steps without provisioning or paying for idle clusters.

name: Catalog Federation (Hive/Glue/Snowflake)
blurb: Expose Glue, Hive, and Snowflake catalogs under one Unity Catalog governance plane during a phased migration.

name: Data Governance Hub
blurb: A single console for data stewards to monitor classification, access, and quality across the member and claims estate.

name: Hive Metastore (legacy)
limitations: Requires legacy table access control for access when using standard access mode compute; workspace-local scope only (not cross-workspace)
blurb: The legacy metadata store the payer is migrating off; no new PHI workloads should land here.

name: Lakehouse Federation
limitations: Read-only (no write support); queries run on both Databricks and remote compute; requires JDBC connectivity to external databases
blurb: Query claims still sitting in a legacy SQL Server or Snowflake without migrating them first, so analysts aren't blocked during migration.

name: Query Federation (11 external DBs)
limitations: Read-only, no write support; queries run on both Databricks and remote compute (not fully pushed down); table-level access controls only
blurb: Join live operational data such as Postgres eligibility to lakehouse claims for a single analytic view.

name: READ METADATA privilege default (CSP)
blurb: Tightens default metadata visibility under the compliance security profile so schema details aren't over-shared.

name: Role-based access / role assumption
blurb: Map enterprise roles directly to Databricks grants for cleaner least-privilege administration.

name: Secrets in Unity Catalog
blurb: Store API keys for payer integrations (clearinghouses, EHRs) as governed UC objects instead of loose workspace secrets.

name: Unity Catalog
limitations: Metastore is region-scoped (cross-region needs Delta Sharing); requires Databricks Runtime 11.3 LTS+; clusters need standard/dedicated access mode; workspace-level groups not supported in GRANT statements; object names max 255 chars
blurb: The single governance layer over every catalog, claim, and member record in the lakehouse. Gives the payer one place to enforce access, lineage, and audit evidence for HIPAA across all workspaces.

name: JDBC Unity Catalog connections
limitations: Read-only, no write support; queries run on both Databricks and remote compute (not fully pushed down)

name: remote_query in compliance security profile
limitations: Read-only, no write support; queries run on both Databricks and remote compute (not fully pushed down)

name: JDBC connections in compliance security profile
limitations: Read-only, no write support; queries run on both Databricks and remote compute (not Databricks-only)

name: Attribute-based access control (ABAC)
blurb: Grant access by attribute — e.g., care-management team or region — instead of maintaining thousands of per-table grants.

name: Audit logs
blurb: Immutable record of who touched PHI and when — the evidence auditors ask for in HIPAA and SOC 2 reviews.

name: Catalogs & schemas
limitations: Object names cannot exceed 255 characters; names cannot contain period, space, forward slash, ASCII control characters, or DELETE character; all object names stored as lowercase; bucketing not supported for Unity Catalog tables
blurb: Isolate data by line of business — Commercial, Medicare, Medicaid — in separate catalogs so entitlements and audit stay clean per segment.

name: Data lineage
blurb: Prove where a member's data flowed end-to-end for HIPAA audits and breach-impact investigations.

name: External locations & storage credentials
blurb: Pin exactly which cloud storage paths may hold PHI and which principals can reach them — the storage boundary for the compliance profile.

name: External tables
limitations: Shallow cloning external tables requires Databricks Runtime 14.2+; partition manipulation commands require partition metadata logging enabled; overwrite mode for non-Delta formats requires CREATE TABLE privilege on schema and ownership or MODIFY privilege
blurb: Register existing S3/ADLS claim extracts in place so legacy EDW landing data is governed without a copy.

name: Governed tags
blurb: Tag columns as PHI/PII so classification and downstream policy follow the data automatically across the catalog.

name: Managed tables (Delta/Iceberg)
limitations: Must use Delta or Iceberg format only; cannot shallow clone between managed and external tables; bucketing not supported; object names cannot exceed 255 characters or contain periods, spaces, slashes, or control characters
blurb: Default governed storage for claims, eligibility, and member tables, with optimization handled by the platform.

name: Row filters & column masks
limitations: Evaluated at query time; cannot nest.
objections: Approved as the standard PHI control.
blurb: The payer's standard minimum-necessary control: mask SSNs and diagnosis codes and filter members by plan or state at query time. Approved as the default PHI guardrail across the enterprise.

name: System tables
blurb: Query usage, access, and billing telemetry to attribute DBU spend to each line of business and feed audit reporting.

name: UDFs in compliance security profile
limitations: Python UDFs not supported in Databricks Runtime 12.2 LTS and below; Scala UDFs not supported in Databricks Runtime 14.1 and below on standard access mode compute; requires Databricks Runtime 11.3 LTS or above for Unity Catalog; requires standard or dedicated access mode

name: Volumes (unstructured)
limitations: Object names cannot exceed 255 characters; special characters (period, space, forward slash, ASCII control characters, DELETE character) not allowed in names; Unity Catalog stores all object names as lowercase
blurb: Govern clinical PDFs, provider contracts, and faxed documents alongside structured data under the same permissions.

name: AI/BI Dashboards
limitations: 15 pages max per dashboard; 100 datasets max per dashboard; 100 widgets max per page; dropdown/multiselect filters limited to 100,000 rendered values; most visualizations truncate at 15,000 rows; table visualizations truncate at 100,000 rows; subscription email attachments limited to 9MB combined
blurb: Governed dashboards for executives and quality teams, built directly on the lakehouse. Approved for internal reporting including HEDIS/Stars measure tracking.

name: AI/BI Genie
limitations: Genie Code has pay-as-you-go pricing after free monthly allowance (effective July 8, 2026); Genie One and Agents free only through January 31, 2027; service principals excluded from free promotion and are billed
objections: Board wants proof UC masks/row filters hold in generated SQL before PHI.
blurb: Natural-language Q&A over governed data so analysts can ask claims and membership questions without writing SQL. Under board review until UC masks and row filters are proven to hold in Genie-generated SQL.

name: Databricks SQL
blurb: The warehouse surface analysts and BI tools use to query governed claims and member data. Approved as the enterprise serving layer for reporting.

name: Metric Views
blurb: Define measures like MLR, PMPM, and denial rate once so every dashboard and Genie answer agrees on the number.

name: Cross-filtering & drill-through
blurb: Let analysts click from a denial-rate trend down to the specific plans or providers driving it.

name: Dataset materialization
limitations: Small datasets (≤100,000 rows or ≤100MB) processed in browser; large datasets (>100,000 rows or >100MB) processed on backend with different query behavior

name: Embedding
limitations: Gated by workspace settings.
blurb: Embed quality dashboards inside internal provider or care-management portals.

name: Subscriptions
limitations: 9MB combined attachment size limit for subscription emails; Excel attachments limited to 100,000 rows; PDF attachments excluded if >9MB; tabular attachments excluded if combined size >9MB
blurb: Email scheduled snapshots of KPIs to leadership without manual exports.

name: CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW metadata preservation
Materialized views & streaming tables
blurb: Pre-compute quality measures and KPIs so dashboards load instantly.

name: New SQL editor
blurb: A faster authoring experience for the payer's analyst community.

name: Pipe syntax & geospatial (H3)
blurb: Analyze provider networks and member geography — e.g., access-to-care distance by region.

name: Query history, profiling & insights
blurb: Diagnose slow analyst queries and attribute warehouse cost by team.

name: SQL alerts
blurb: Notify teams when a metric breaches a threshold — e.g., claims backlog or denial rate spikes.

name: SQL scripting / stored procedures
blurb: Port legacy EDW stored procedures for claims processing into governed SQL.

name: SQL warehouses (serverless/pro/classic)
blurb: Elastic SQL compute for BI dashboards and ad-hoc analyst queries, scaled to demand.

name: Genie One skill sharing with Unity Gateway
Data Science Agent
blurb: Accelerate exploratory data science on claims and clinical datasets.

name: Genie Agents
blurb: Curated per-domain assistants — e.g., a claims agent and an eligibility agent.

name: Genie Code
limitations: Pay-as-you-go pricing model with per-user free monthly allowance starting July 8, 2026; account admin budget management required
blurb: Generate and run analysis code from natural language for power analysts.

name: Genie One
limitations: Service principal usage is billed (not included in free promotion through January 31, 2027)
blurb: A single conversational entry point across the payer's governed data domains.

name: Genie scheduled tasks
blurb: Run recurring natural-language questions (e.g., a weekly denial summary) on a schedule.

name: Automatic cluster updates
limitations: Does not apply to serverless compute resources; only applies to classic compute plane resources; requires Enterprise pricing tier; adds Enhanced Security and Compliance add-on cost; only configurable by account admins from account console
blurb: Keep compute patched automatically so security fixes land without manual effort.

name: Compliance security profile
limitations: Account-level Genie One does not aggregate data from workspaces with compliance security profile enabled; enforces specific instance types for inter-node encryption; Databricks identities stored in US and each workspace region
objections: Required for all PHI workloads — permanent once enabled.
blurb: The master switch that puts a workspace into HIPAA/PCI/FedRAMP posture with hardened images and monitoring. Required for every PHI workload and permanent once enabled.

name: Customer-managed VPC
limitations: Cannot migrate existing workspace from Databricks-managed VPC to customer-managed VPC; must be configured at workspace creation; Databricks-managed VPC will be deprecated for new classic workspaces in future release
objections: Databricks-managed VPC deprecating for new classic workspaces.
blurb: Run Databricks inside the payer's own network with its existing controls and monitoring.

name: Customer-managed keys (CMK)
limitations: Requires Enterprise tier; serverless workspaces only support managed services CMK use case; setting up CMK for managed services causes certain fields in metastore query history system table to be affected
blurb: Encrypt PHI with keys the payer owns and can revoke. Approved as a required control for regulated data at rest.

name: Encryption in transit / worker-node
limitations: Requires Enterprise plan; init script approach exposes shared secret to any user with DBFS access; cluster restart required when rotating keystore; Spark workers may fail to authenticate if secret inconsistent
blurb: Encrypt data moving between cluster nodes, closing an often-audited gap for PHI.

name: Enhanced Security Monitoring
limitations: Classic compute plane only; serverless compute resources (serverless SQL warehouses) do not receive enhanced monitoring; monitoring agents cannot be disabled
blurb: Adds malware, file-integrity, and vulnerability monitoring on compute handling PHI. Approved as part of the hardened security posture.

name: IP access lists
limitations: Requires Enterprise pricing tier; does not apply to PrivateLink private IP addresses (only public IPs); blocking private IPs from PrivateLink requires AWS Network Firewall
blurb: Restrict workspace access to the payer's corporate and VPN ranges.

name: Network Connectivity Config (NCC) / PSC
blurb: Give serverless workloads stable, firewalled egress so partner allowlists stay simple and secure.

name: PrivateLink (front-end & back-end)
limitations: Dual PrivateLink needed for full private path.
blurb: Keep all traffic to and from Databricks on the private network, off the public internet. Approved as a core requirement for the payer's PHI environment.

name: SSO / SCIM
limitations: Requires Premium plan or above; maximum 10,000 combined users and service principals per account/workspace; maximum 5,000 groups per account/workspace; does not support syncing service principals or nested groups (use automatic identity management instead)
blurb: Centralize login and automatic deprovisioning through the payer's identity provider. Approved as a required access control.

name: Secret management
limitations: Workspace admins, secret creators, and users with granted permissions can access and read secrets; secret redaction in notebook outputs cannot be fully guaranteed; secret scope names are readable by all users in the workspace; secret scope names limited to 128 characters
blurb: Keep credentials for clearinghouses and EHR integrations out of notebooks and code.

name: Secure Cluster Connectivity (NPIP)
blurb: Compute runs with no public IP addresses, a baseline network control for PHI. Approved as a required posture for all production workspaces.

name: Serverless egress controls / firewall
limitations: Firewall rules must be set explicitly; creating resource firewall affects both serverless and classic compute plane connectivity
blurb: Restrict where serverless workloads can send data, preventing accidental PHI egress.

name: FedRAMP High (GovCloud)
limitations: GovCloud region only; requires Enhanced Security and Compliance add-on (additional charges); account-level Genie One does not aggregate data from compliant workspaces
blurb: Relevant only if the payer serves government lines of business in GovCloud.

name: HIPAA
limitations: Requires Enhanced Security and Compliance add-on (additional charges); BAA agreement with Databricks required before processing PHI; Account-level Genie One does not aggregate data from compliant workspaces; enforced instance types for inter-node encryption
blurb: The specific profile the payer runs for all protected health information workloads.

name: PCI-DSS
limitations: Requires Enhanced Security and Compliance add-on (additional cost); enforces specific instance types for inter-node encryption; Account-level Genie One does not aggregate data from workspaces with compliance security profile enabled
blurb: Available if payment-card data ever enters a workspace, e.g., premium billing.

name: Antivirus & malware detection
limitations: Only applies to classic compute plane (clusters, non-serverless SQL warehouses); does not apply to serverless compute; scans only cluster VMs, not resources outside VMs; cannot disable the agent
blurb: Scan compute nodes for malware as part of the compliance posture.

name: File integrity monitoring
limitations: Only applies to classic compute plane (clusters, non-serverless SQL warehouses); does not apply to serverless compute; monitoring agent cannot be disabled; runs on worker VM only
blurb: Detect unauthorized changes to system files on PHI compute.

name: Vulnerability scanning
limitations: Applies only to classic compute plane resources (clusters, non-serverless SQL warehouses); serverless compute resources do not receive vulnerability scanning; scanning occurs in representative images in Databricks environments, not individual customer workspaces
blurb: Continuously surface vulnerabilities on cluster images for remediation.

name: Context-based ingress policies for Private Link
CMK for query history
limitations: Requires Enterprise tier; setting up CMK for managed services causes certain fields in the metastore's query history system table to be affected

name: OAuth custom identity claims for service principals
Clean Rooms
limitations: Max 10 collaborators; requires serverless workspace; uses default storage; classic compute cannot interact with Clean Rooms data; credential vending not supported for external systems
objections: Confirm PHI handling in multi-party outputs.
blurb: Run joint analytics with providers or partners where neither side exposes its raw data. Under review to confirm PHI handling in multi-party outputs.

name: Databricks Marketplace
blurb: Acquire third-party datasets — e.g., provider directories or SDOH data — to enrich payer analytics. One governed channel for external data.

name: Delta Sharing / Open Sharing
limitations: Modes differ by recipient type; see sub-features.
blurb: Share governed data with providers, vendors, and partners without copying or FTP. The payer's standard for secure, auditable external data exchange.

name: Approved notebooks
blurb: Only vetted code runs in the clean room, protecting both parties' data.

name: Collaborators
blurb: Add provider or vendor partners to a governed, privacy-preserving analysis.

name: Output tables
blurb: Share only the aggregated results, never the underlying member records.

name: Default Storage Sharing
blurb: Simplifies sharing data that lives in Databricks-managed storage.

name: Mode: Databricks-to-Databricks
limitations: Does not require credential files (authentication handled through Databricks)
blurb: Share live data instantly with partners who also run Databricks — no file transfers.

name: Mode: Databricks-to-Open (bearer/OIDC)
limitations: Metadata file doesn't automatically update with latest snapshot in Snowflake, requires auto-refresh or manual refreshes; R2 not supported in Snowflake; All Iceberg client limitations apply
objections: Approved for de-identified data only, pending DLP egress review.
blurb: Share with partners on any platform via open protocol. Approved for de-identified data only, pending a DLP egress review.

name: SecureConnect (firewall-protected sharing)
objections: Expanded billing for private/public connectivity coming.
blurb: Adds firewall-protected private connectivity to data sharing for stricter network control.

name: Share AI models
limitations: Metadata file doesn't automatically update with latest snapshot in Snowflake, requires auto-refresh or manual refreshes; R2 not supported; All Iceberg client limitations apply
blurb: Distribute a trained model to a partner or affiliate under governance.

name: Share notebooks
limitations: Databricks-to-Databricks only.
blurb: Hand analysis notebooks to a Databricks partner for joint analytics work.

name: Share tables / streaming tables
limitations: Snowflake Iceberg REST Catalog: metadata file doesn't automatically update with latest snapshot, requires auto-refresh or manual refreshes; R2 not supported; all Iceberg client limitations apply
blurb: Share curated claims or quality tables, including continuously updated ones.

name: Share views (with masks/filters)
limitations: Metadata file doesn't automatically update with latest snapshot in Snowflake (requires auto-refresh or manual refresh); R2 not supported; All Iceberg client limitations apply
blurb: Share only a masked, filtered slice of a table so partners never see full PHI.

name: Share volumes
limitations: D2D mode; open mode limited.
blurb: Share document sets such as provider packets through governed volumes.

name: Shares & recipients
limitations: Snowflake Iceberg REST Catalog: metadata file doesn't automatically update with latest snapshot, requires auto-refresh or manual refreshes; R2 not supported; all Iceberg client limitations apply
blurb: Define exactly which datasets each external recipient can see, with full audit.

name: Datasets
blurb: Subscribe to reference and enrichment datasets directly into the lakehouse.

name: Partner Connect
limitations: Only available for select Databricks technology partners; requires manual connection as alternative if partner not in Partner Connect program
blurb: Connect validated partner tools to the platform with minimal setup.

name: Apache Iceberg
blurb: Open table format support so partners and external engines can read payer data without lock-in. Key for provider and vendor interoperability.

name: Automatic Change Data Feed
blurb: Turns on change tracking automatically so downstream claims consumers always get incremental updates.

name: Delta Lake
blurb: The ACID storage format under every claims and member table, giving reliable upserts, deletes, and time travel. Approved as the payer's default table format.

name: Lakebase (Postgres OLTP)
limitations: Region availability is limited; feature appears to be in Public Preview for some capabilities (Postgres changes storage)
blurb: A managed Postgres database for powering member-facing apps and low-latency serving next to the lakehouse. Under board review for backup, retention, and PHI-at-rest handling.

name: Variant shredding (auto)
blurb: Auto-optimizes queries over semi-structured FHIR/JSON data for faster access with no manual tuning.

name: Variant type (semi-structured)
limitations: Cannot partition, cluster, group by, order by, or use DISTINCT on variant columns; no SQL set operators (INTERSECT, UNION, EXCEPT); no minValues/maxValues statistics; 128 MiB max value size (16 MiB in Runtime 17.1 and below); requires Runtime 15.4 LTS or above
blurb: Store and query semi-structured payloads like FHIR resources or EDI segments without flattening them first.

name: Change Data Feed (CDF)
blurb: Capture row-level changes to propagate claims corrections downstream incrementally.

name: Column mapping
limitations: Disables CDF / incremental manifests.
blurb: Rename or reorder columns without rewriting data as source schemas evolve.

name: Deletion vectors
limitations: Interacts with external Iceberg readers.
blurb: Efficiently delete individual member records — useful for right-to-delete and correction workflows.

name: Liquid clustering
limitations: Clustering columns fixed at creation.
blurb: Keep large claims tables fast to query without manual partition tuning.

name: Schema enforcement & data skipping
blurb: Reject malformed claims writes and skip irrelevant files for faster, safer queries.

name: Time travel
blurb: Query a table as of a prior date to reproduce a report or investigate a data issue.

name: VACUUM
limitations: LITE mode in Public Preview.
blurb: Reclaim storage and help enforce PHI retention by physically removing old files.

name: External Iceberg reads
blurb: Read Iceberg tables produced by other systems without copying them in.

name: Iceberg REST Catalog (IRC)
blurb: Let external engines discover governed payer tables through a standard catalog API.

name: Iceberg v3
blurb: Use the latest Iceberg spec features for richer interoperability.

name: Managed Iceberg tables
blurb: Create fully managed Iceberg tables when partners standardize on Iceberg.

name: UniForm (Iceberg/Delta)
limitations: Write ops limited.
blurb: Expose one physical table as both Delta and Iceberg so every consumer can read it.

name: Autoscaling upgrade
blurb: Scale the serving database automatically with member-portal traffic spikes.

name: Branching
blurb: Spin up isolated database copies for testing app changes without touching production member data.

name: Synced tables
blurb: Automatically mirror a governed lakehouse table into Postgres for fast app lookups.
